Christopher Columbus

Blockchain technology is a digital record-keeping system that works without a central authority, ensuring that transactions are secure and visible to everyone involved. Imagine a digital notebook where each page (called a "block") holds a list of recent transactions. Once a page is filled and verified by the network, it is permanently sealed and cannot be changed or erased. This permanence is protected by advanced mathematical codes that link each page securely to the one before it. Because every page is tied to the previous one, it is extremely difficult for anyone to alter past records or commit fraud, making the entire system highly trustworthy and resistant to tampering.
